title: Test, debug, and build in a real browser
description: An AI that uses your app, not just reads your code: automated QA, debugging with the console open, websites with real images, and fast web data extraction.
introduction: Most AI coding tools can read your code. Strawberry can also use your app: click through it in a real browser, watch the console and the network, and tell you exactly what broke.
Its harness is built for the web, so it's fast at the things other tools find awkward. Pulling thousands of rows out of a website often takes a minute instead of an hour.

blocks.text: Not sure where to start? Strawberry is free to download. Ask your companion to look at your work and suggest the first thing worth handing over.

sections.title: Automated QA on your staging site

blocks.text: Point Strawberry at the flows that matter. It clicks through them like a user and reports what breaks, with screenshots and steps to reproduce. Put it on a Routine and it checks every morning.

demo.title: Staging smoke test
steps: Signed up as a new user

blocks.text: Strawberry reads the console, the network requests, and the page itself, so it can tell a broken API response from a broken button.

demo.prompt: Why does the save button do nothing on /settings?
steps: Missing timezone field in the request

blocks.text: Give it your brand, or a site whose style you like, and it builds pages with real screenshots or generated images instead of grey boxes.

demo.prompt: Build a landing page for our API in the style of linear.app

sections.title: Scrape any site into a spreadsheet

blocks.text: Many sites load their data through their own requests. Strawberry reads those directly, so a directory with thousands of rows becomes a clean spreadsheet quickly and cheaply.

demo.prompt: Get every exhibitor from this conference site into a sheet
steps: Sheet ready with a source on every row

items.context: Say which fields you need and get a checked sample before the full run.

blocks.text: Before a feature, Strawberry reads the docs, changelogs, and issue threads, and comes back with the approach, the gotchas, and the APIs you'll need.

demo.prompt: How should we add passkeys to our Next.js login?
steps: Read 14 docs pages and 6 GitHub issues

sections.title: Why a browser, not a chatbot

blocks.text: Chat assistants can't see your running app. Strawberry can.

items: It drives a real browser, including localhost and staging, and reads the console and network as it goes.
It works across many tabs at once instead of one step at a time.
You can watch every tab and take over at any point.

blocks.text: In our test of 12 real-world tasks, Strawberry scored 99.2 out of 100. Perplexity's Comet scored 90.8 and ChatGPT Atlas 73.3.

items: Find typos, broken links, and console errors across a whole site.
Create or review a pull request.
File a bug with evidence and steps to reproduce.
Turn support tickets, calls, and reviews into product insight.

blocks.text: Save a QA flow as a team skill and every engineer's companion runs it the same way. Put the nightly check on a Routine and the team hears about regressions before customers do.
